block.name: master_axi_monitor
block.comment: Monitor transactions on the AXI bus.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_ENABLE
register.comment: Enable the AXI monitor. Enabled by default because turning it on at any point would mean probably missing something and getting out of sync.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_ID_WRITE_MASK
register.comment: Bitfield indicating from which AXI ID(s) bits to to check in burst transactions. If 0, all masters are monitored. If mask is non-zero then if a matching value in AXI_MON_ID_VALUE for the bits set here is true then monitoring occurs.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_ID_WRITE_VALUE
register.comment: Value to match the incoming AXI ID against.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_ID_READ_MASK
register.comment: Bitfield indicating from which AXI ID(s) bits to to check in burst transactions. If 0, all masters are monitored. If mask is non-zero then if a matching value in AXI_MON_ID_VALUE for the bits set here is true then monitoring occurs.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_ID_READ_VALUE
register.comment: Value to match the incoming AXI ID against.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_INST_READ_BURST_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of read burst transactions on the AXI read channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_INST_READ_BYTE_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of bytes transferred in the read burst transactions on the AXI read channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_INST_WRITE_BURST_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of write burst transactions on the AXI read channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_INST_WRITE_BYTE_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of bytes transferred in the write burst transactions on the AXI write channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_DATA_READ_BURST_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of read burst transactions on the AXI read channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_DATA_READ_BYTE_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of bytes transferred in the read burst transactions on the AXI read channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_DATA_WRITE_BURST_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of write burst transactions on the AXI read channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_DATA_WRITE_BYTE_COUNT
register.comment: Count of the number of bytes transferred in the write burst transactions on the AXI write channel.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_OUTSTANDING_STATUS
register.comment: Dynamic status of outstanding reads/writes

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_OUTSTANDING_STATUS_MAX
register.comment: Maximum value of outstanding reads/writes since last clear.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_OUTSTANDING_STATUS_MAX_CLEAR
register.comment: Clear status of outstanding reads/writes

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_SPARSE_WRITE_COUNT
register.comment: Count of Synopsys PCIE-incompatible sparse write bursts that occurred for the given ID.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_SPARSE_WRITE_COUNT_CLEAR
register.comment: Clear count of sparse writes.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_STATE
register.comment: Current state of PCIE write burst tracking.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_STATE_CLEAR
register.comment: Reset the state of PCIE write burst tracking.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_INT_CONFIG
register.comment: Interrupt configuration.

register.name: MASTER_AXI_MON_INT_LIMIT
register.comment: Limit to test against for interrupt generation

register.comment: PCIe Link IP Version(5.97a)

register.name: PCIE_LINK_RESET
register.comment: PCIe Link controller reset controls

register.name: PCIE_LINK_DBI_RO_WR_DISABLE
register.comment: DBI Read-only Write Disable<br> 0: MISC_CONTROL_1_OFF.DBI_RO_WR_EN register field is read-write.<br> 1: MISC_CONTROL_1_OFF.DBI_RO_WR_EN register field is forced to 0 and is read-only

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CTRL
register.comment: PCIE link control

register.name: PCIE_LINK_SYS_INT
register.comment: When set, the controller generates an Assert_INTA Legacy Interrupt Message. When unset, the controller generates a Deassert_INTA Legacy Interrupt Message.

register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Disable interrupt/read enable status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ0_ENABLE
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Enable interrupt/read enable status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ0_CLEAR
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Clear interrupt/read pending interrupt status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ0_EDGE
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Set level/edge config - 0=level 1=edge

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ0_INVERT
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Set invert option - 0=normal 1=invert

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ0_RAW
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Read the raw interrupt status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ1_DISABLE
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Disable interrupt/read enable status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ1_ENABLE
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Enable interrupt/read enable status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ1_CLEAR
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Clear interrupt/read pending interrupt status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ1_EDGE
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Set level/edge config - 0=level 1=edge

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ1_INVERT
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Set invert option - 0=normal 1=invert

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IRQ1_RAW
register.comment: Interrupt requests from PCIe link controller - Read the raw interrupt status

register.name: PCIE_LINK_MSI_SET_PENDING_BIT_ARRAY
register.comment: Writing a 1 to each bit latches a bit in the pending bit array for operation. LSB has priority.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_MSI_CLEAR_PENDING_BIT_ARRAY
register.comment: Writing a 1 in each bit clears a 1 to a 0 in the pending bit array.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_MSI_TC

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CFG
register.comment: Link config and BAR status.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CFG_PBUS_NUM

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CFG_PBUS_DEV_NUM
register.comment: The device number assigned to the function

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CFG_PHY_CONTROL

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CFG_LTR_MAX_LATENCY
register.comment: The concatenated contents of 'LTR Max No-Snoop Latency Register' and 'LTR Max Snoop Latency Register'. The 'LTR Max Snoop Latency' of function 0 occupies the lower 16-bits

register.name: PCIE_LINK_PM_CONTROL

register.name: PCIE_LINK_PM_STATUS

register.name: PCIE_LINK_CXPL_DEBUG_INFO_EI

register.name: PCIE_LINK_IER

register.name: PCIE_LINK_DEBUG_SOURCE[0]

register.name: PCIE_LINK_DEBUG_SOURCE[1]
register.comment: Select the 32bit output on DEBUG_OUT[i] on the PCIE module

register.name: PCIE_LINK_DEBUG_SOURCE[2]
register.comment: Select the 32bit output on DEBUG_OUT[i] on the PCIE module

register.name: PCIE_LINK_DEBUG_SOURCE[3]
register.comment: Select the 32bit output on DEBUG_OUT[i] on the PCIE module

register.name: PCIE_LINK_LTR_MSG_REQ
register.comment: Request to send a LTR Message. Set to trigger sending of message. Reads back 1 when message sending pending. Reads back as 0 when message sent.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_LTR_MSG_LATENCY
register.comment: LTR message that your application is requesting to send. The message format is defined in the PCI Express Specification.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_LTR_MSG_FUNC_NUM
register.comment: Do NOT use this - now provides PCIE_LINK_PM_APP_XFER_PENDING_CA55 function

register.name: PCIE_LINK_RADM_MSG_REQ_ID
register.comment: The requester ID of the received message.<br> Valid when any of {RADM_VENDOR_MSG, RADM_MSG_UNLOCK, RADM_PM_PME, RADM_PM_TURNOFF, RADM_MSG_OBFF, RADM_MSG_IDLE, RADM_MSG_CPU_ACTIVE} are asserted

register.name: PCIE_LINK_RADM_MSG_PAYLOAD[0]
register.comment: Received message header information (Lower, Upper words)

register.name: PCIE_LINK_RADM_MSG_PAYLOAD[1]
register.comment: Received message header information (Lower, Upper words)

register.name: PCIE_LINK_RADM_Q_NOT_EMPTY
register.comment: Level indicating that the receive queues contain TLP header/data.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_RADM_TIMEOUT
register.comment: Receive Control/CPL Timeout signalling

register.name: PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_REQ
register.comment: Request to send a vendor-defined Message. Set to trigger sending of message. Reads back 1 when message sending pending. Reads back as 0 when message sent.

register.name: PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_0
register.comment: Vendor Message Fields (bank 0). All validated by PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_REQ=1

register.name: PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_1
register.comment: Vendor Message Fields (bank 1). All validated by PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_REQ=1

register.name: PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_DATA[0]
register.comment: Third and fourth dwords of the Vendor Defined Message header where:<br> Bytes 8-11 ( third header dword) = ven_msg_data[63:32]<br> Bytes 12-15 (fourth header dword) = ven_msg_data[31:0], where ven_msg_data[7:0] = byte 15

register.name: PCIE_LINK_VEN_MSG_DATA[1]
register.comment: Third and fourth dwords of the Vendor Defined Message header where:<br> Bytes 8-11 ( third header dword) = ven_msg_data[63:32]<br> Bytes 12-15 (fourth header dword) = ven_msg_data[31:0], where ven_msg_data[7:0] = byte 15

register.name: WATCHDOG_ENABLE
register.comment: Writing '1' enables the watchdog regardless of its previous state and resets its state machine to WATCHDOG_STATUS_FSM_ENABLED.

register.name: WATCHDOG_DISABLE
register.comment: Writing the 3 disable codes in sequence to this register will disable the watchdog. Writing WATCHDOG_DEBUG_CODE3 instead of WATCHDOG_DISABLE_CODE3 will set the watchdog into debug mode. Each correct code written will advance the WATCHDOG_STATUS by 1 until it reaches 3. A status of 3 indicates that the watchdog has been disabled A status of 4 indicates that the watchdog is in debug mode. If an incorrect code is written at any time, the status will revert to 0 (enabled). The watchdog will not stop counting down until all three codes have been written correctly.

register.name: WATCHDOG_DELAY
register.comment: This is the reset value for the watchdog countdown. The reset value is 0xFFFF which allows a countdown period of 2 seconds. The maximum value of 0xFFFFFFFF allows for a sleep time of around 37 hours

register.name: WATCHDOG_KICK
register.comment: Writing to this register causes the countdown value to be reset to the value stored in WATCHDOG_DELAY. WATCHDOG_DELAY is captured into the slow clock domain after a cycle or two. The register fields WATCHDOG_STATUS_KICK_PENDING and WATCHDOG_STATUS_SLOW_KICK_PENDING indicate if this register has already been written and an update is currently pending. Writing this register toggles a flag inside the watchdog logic so writing it a second time before the first has successfully propagated will clear the toggle and cancel the kick.

register.name: WPAN_PP_PROC_REMAP_RGN1_OVERRIDE_EN
register.comment: SET TO 1 BEFORE WPAN M7 BOOT! Apply a fixed offset to the WPAN CPU remapper region 1 which maps in the MIF memory region at 0x9000_0000. The fixed offset means that those addresses are all shifted up to the 0xA000_0000 region which is an invalid region in the WPAN NIC-400. Once the MPU is configured correctly this override can be disabled and accesses to 0x9000_0000 can be allowed again.

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_DDB_LEVEL_2_DATA_LENGTH

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_TIMEOUT_INIT_VALUE
register.comment: SPMI Timeout(96us) Timer Initial Value. Please refer to SCLKint Freq and connect. 0x0 : 2 Cycle, 0x1 : 3 Cycle, 0x2 : 4 Cycle ... Do not enter the Maximum Value. Init Value based on 26Mhz Clock (SCLK_INT) (2496 cycles so 2494 init value)

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_MAX_FREQ

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_SW_RESET_FSM
register.comment: Writing to this register will reset the iternal FSM

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_SW_RESET_IO
register.comment: Writing to this register will reset the IO (SCLK, SDATA)

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_SW_RESET_SFR
register.comment: Writing to this register will reset the internal SFR (Not the Inbound/Outbound Ports)

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_TIMEOUT_CONDITION
register.comment: This bit indicates the reset condition of the timeout counter. Basically, the timeout counter is initialized only by SCLK. If this bit is enabled, timeout counter is also initialized by SDATA. 0 : SCLK only, 1: SCLK and SDATA

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_TIMEOUT
register.comment: This bit indicates that the SPMI is currently timeout

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_NACK_RESPONSE
register.comment: When the write command enters, refer to this bit for ACK/NACK response. Please change it only if it is not spmi_busy == 1 1 : NACK 0 : ACK

register.name: SPMI_SLAVE_BUSY
register.comment: This bit indicates that the SPMI is busy

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_ADDR_CTRL_MPORT_I0
register.comment: ZIPPY (MULTIPORT)Remote register access address and controls. The bottom 16 bits of this register (PSEL and ADDR) are actually the bottom 16 bits of the byte address of the RFIC register to be accessed (from HTML docs for example)

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_WRITE_DATA_MPORT_I0
register.comment: ZIPPY (MULTIPORT) Data to write to remote register over ZIPPY. Only the number of bytes specified in the ZIPPY_BB_WIDTH field are transferred. Unwritten bytes are unchanged, if the destination register is larger than the number of bytes written

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_WRITE_DATA_MASK_MPORT_I0
register.comment: ZIPPY (MULTIPORT) Any bits cleared in this register will not be written at the destination register. Action is performed by doing a automatic Read-Modify-Write operation. There is no Read-interrupt on completion however the READ data (in the Read-Modify-Write cycle) is saved in the ZIPPY_BB_READ_DATA_ register.

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_READ_DATA_MPORT_I0
register.comment: ZIPPY (MULTIPORT) Data returned from the remote register over ZIPPY. Only the number of bytes specified in the ZIPPY_BB_WIDTH field are transferred

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_INT_MPORT_DISABLE_I0

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_INT_MPORT_CLEAR_I0
register.comment: ZIPPY (MultiPORT) Interrupt controller. - Clear interrupt/read pending interrupt status

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_INT_MPORT_RAW_I0
register.comment: ZIPPY (MultiPORT) Interrupt controller. - Read incoming interrupt status

register.name: ZIPPY_BB_LATENCY_MPORT_I0
register.comment: Zippy transfer latency
